The fine print: clauses that qualify the headline promises.
The fee framing: no platform fees, but spreads embedded in every trade.
The support story: around-the-clock coverage claimed, exact figures conflicting.
The geo-restrictions: two lists on the page that do not agree.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Create the account with your contact details, then verify it through the emailed link.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Make the US$250 first deposit using any of the listed payment methods.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your limits, pick a trading mode and let the demo build your confidence first.

pros: No platform fees on top of spreads.
Automatic and manual modes.
Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
cons: No independent audit of the models.
Registration details not stated up front.
The demo claim buried in the signup flow.
redFlags: Performance language with no dates attached.
A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
US$250, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.

bottomLine: What we found is a real service wrapped in marketing that outruns its own fine print. Trade the service, not the marketing.
The verdict holds at 4.5: research it, demo it, and if you fund it, fund the minimum. The platform earns a careful start, not blind trust.
